# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

Unit tests cover JS logic with mocks, but a Teammate agent's full wiring
(preJSAction → input context → preCliJSAction → CLI → postJSAction) can also
be exercised against **real Jira/Confluence/etc.** without invoking the real
AI CLI (`scripts/run-agent.sh`). Two dmtools features make this possible:

1. **CLI param overrides** — `dmtools run <config.json> --key value` patches
   the `params` block. Values that look like JSON arrays/objects are parsed as
   JSON, so even `cliCommands` and `customParams` can be overridden:

   ```bash
   dmtools run agents/story_solution.json \
     --inputJql "key = PROJ-123" \
     --cliCommands '["/path/to/fake_cli.sh"]' \
     --customParams '{"contentOutput":{"target":"confluence","space":"DOC","parentPageId":"123456"}}' \
     --alwaysPostComments false \
     --cleanupInputFolder false
   ```

2. **A fake CLI script** that mimics the agent contract: read `input/`, write
   `outputs/response.md` (and any other files the post-action expects, e.g.
   `outputs/confluence_replies.json`). Keep it outside the repo (it is
   project- and machine-specific):

   ```bash
   #!/bin/bash
   set -e
   mkdir -p outputs
   printf '# Fake output\n\nGenerated by the e2e fake CLI.\n' > outputs/response.md
   ```

Rules for live e2e runs:

- **Never commit live-e2e configs or scripts to this repo** — they contain
  real ticket keys, page IDs and space keys, which violates the
  project-agnostic rule. Keep them in a scratch directory or pass everything
  via CLI overrides.
- Run against **dedicated garbage objects** (a test ticket and a test
  Confluence page clearly marked "safe to delete"), never real work items.
- Pass `--cleanupInputFolder false` so you can inspect `input/<KEY>/`
  afterwards, and `--alwaysPostComments false` to keep the test ticket quiet.
- After the run, verify the side effects directly (e.g. `jira_get_ticket`,
  `confluence_content_by_id`, `confluence_get_page_inline_comments`) rather
  than trusting the job log.

## Conventions

### No project-specific content — STRICT RULE

**This is a public, product-agnostic repository. NEVER commit anything company- or customer-specific here.** Violations are a fireable offense and require history rewrite.

Forbidden anywhere in this repo (code, comments, prompts, instructions, tests, docs, commit messages):

- Company, customer, or product names
- Internal hostnames, URLs, IPs, Jira/Confluence links, real ticket keys
- Internal label/branch/repo naming conventions tied to one organization
- File paths pointing to internal repos, internal registry URLs
- Sample data copied from real internal systems

Everything here must be **generic and configurable**: names like `example.com`, `PROJ-123`, `acme`; behavior driven by `customParams` / `.dmtools/config.js` in the consuming repo. Project context goes in the target repo's `.dmtools/config.js` or the corporate orchestrator repo — never here.

**Before every commit**: re-read your diff and check it against this list.

### Agent config structure
- `metadata.contextId` identifies the workflow (used for config composition lookups).
- `preJSAction` / `preCliJSAction` / `postJSAction` — GraalJS hooks that run before/after the CLI agent.
- `cliPrompt` — path to the main prompt markdown.
- `cliPrompts` — additional prompt files appended to the CLI agent input.
- `cliCommands` — shell scripts invoked by dmtools to run the AI CLI.

### Label-based idempotency
SM rules use `skipIfLabel` / `addLabel` to prevent re-processing tickets. When adding new rules, always include an idempotency label.

### SCM abstraction
Use `js/common/scm.js` (via `configLoader.createScm(config)`) instead of calling `github_*` or `ado_*` globals directly. This keeps agents portable between GitHub and Azure DevOps.

### Config composition
Project repos customize agent behavior through `.dmtools/config.js` fields:
- `cliPrompts.<contextId>` — append prompt files to a specific agent's CLI input
- `cliPromptOverrides.<contextId>` — replace the entry prompt for a specific agent
- `additionalInstructions.<contextId>` — append to `agentParams.instructions` for a specific agent
- `instructionOverrides.<contextId>` — replace `agentParams.instructions` for a specific agent
- `agentParamPatches.<contextId>` — patch `agentParams` fields for a specific agent
- `globalCliPrompts` — prompt files appended to **every** agent's CLI input (inject-to-all)
- `globalAdditionalInstructions` — instruction files appended to **every** agent's `agentParams.instructions`

**Example — inject codegraph into all agents without repeating per context:**
```js
// .dmtools/config.js
module.exports = {
    globalCliPrompts: [
        './agents/instructions/common/codegraph_tools.md'
    ],
    cliPrompts: {
        story_development: ['./.dmtools/prompts/development_focus.md'],
        pr_review:         ['./.dmtools/prompts/review_focus.md']
        // codegraph_tools.md is injected automatically into all agents above
    }
};
```

Global entries are merged **after** per-agent entries so they always appear last.

### SM rules override and custom agents
`js/smAgent.js` supports full and partial SM customization from `.dmtools/config.js`.

**Precedence**
- Base rules come from `sm.json` (`jobParams.rules`)
- If `config.smRules` is set, it **fully replaces** base rules
- If `config.smRuleOverrides` is set, it patches rules by `configFile`

**Common use cases**
- Disable most default rules and keep only one:
```js
module.exports = {
  smRuleOverrides: {
    "agents/story_questions.json": { enabled: true },
    "agents/story_development.json": { enabled: false },
    "agents/pr_review.json": { enabled: false }
  }
};
```

- Full replacement with custom agents:
```js
module.exports = {
  smRules: [
    {
      description: "Run only custom intake flow",
      jql: "project = {jiraProject} AND issuetype = Story AND status = 'To Do'",
      configFile: "agents/my_custom_intake.json",
      skipIfLabel: "sm_my_custom_intake_triggered",
      addLabel: "sm_my_custom_intake_triggered",
      enabled: true
    }
  ]
};
```

**Rule fields supported by SM**
- `description`, `jql`, `configFile` (required for practical execution)
- `enabled` (set `false` to disable)
- `skipIfLabel` / `skipIfLabels`, `addLabel`
- `targetStatus`, `limit`, `localExecution`
- `configPath` (per-rule project config override for multi-project orchestration)

### Figma design lookup
Any agent that writes or reviews requirements-facing content (questions, descriptions, acceptance criteria, solution/design analysis, dev/test scoping) must treat the linked Figma design as a primary source, not an optional nice-to-have — a story/question/AC that ignores an available design is incomplete, the same way ignoring the code would be.

- **If a ticket/story already links a specific Figma file or node** (a `/file/` or `/design/` URL, optionally with `node-id`): open it directly with `figma_get_file_structure` / `figma_get_layers` / `figma_download_image_of_file` (see `instructions/common/media_handling.md`) before writing output.
- **If only a team- or project-level Figma URL is known** (e.g. a `.../team/<teamId>/...` "files" listing link, typically stored as project config rather than on the ticket itself): resolve it top-down with `figma_list_team_projects` → `figma_list_project_files` to find the file matching the current feature/epic, then drill into it as above. Match by file name against the feature/epic name; if no file name matches, say so explicitly rather than silently skipping the design check.
- **If the design is genuinely unavailable** (no link resolves, access error, no matching file after searching): say so explicitly in the output instead of proceeding as if no design existed — this is the same "unavailable artifact" handling already required by `instructions/common/acceptance_criteria_quality.md`.
- Never fabricate UI/UX details (copy, layout, states) that should come from Figma — pull them from the design or ask a question, don't guess.
- This is process guidance, not a project config — the actual team/project URLs and file-naming convention for a given product live in that product's `.dmtools/instructions/goal/goal.md` or `.dmtools/config.js`, never here.

### Output JSON discipline
When agents produce JSON output files, keep them compact (status, IDs, paths, short summaries). Put large text in separate `.md` files and reference them by path.

### Path stability
Do not rename or move root `*.json` config files — CI workflows and Jira automations reference them by path. Safe refactors: splitting prompt markdown, adding instruction files, adding `cliPrompts` composition in target repos.

# Draft issue 02 — AI failure-analyzer leg: classify repeated failures before re-dispatching (transient vs broken)

Effort: L · Blocked-by: 01 (consumes the contextual failure data)
Config knob: `failureAnalysis.afterFailures` in the SM config (default 4;
owner range 3–5). This changes loop-control behavior for every dev leg —
hence the strict scripted-test matrix below.

## Problem

The SM re-dispatches failed legs unconditionally. That is correct for
transient causes (network outages, runner glitches, API quota — retrying is
the system's resilience and must never require human input to continue).
But when the failure is **deterministic** (repo state, pipeline config,
setup code), retrying burns a runner every few minutes forever — in the
2026-11-04 outage (see **#1360** / **#1358**) 15 legs failed identically
over ~10 hours before a human noticed the pattern.

A dumb signature-count circuit breaker is explicitly rejected (owner
decision, 2026-11-05): identical-looking failures can be transient, so a
counter must never be what stops the loop. Only an agent that READS the
failures and UNDERSTANDS the cause may stop re-dispatching.

## Proposed change

Add an **analyzer leg** to the SM's failure path:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    F[leg fails] --> R[contextual report: phase + step + excerpt + count - issue 01]
    R --> C{consecutive same-signature failures >= afterFailures?}
    C -- no --> D[blind re-dispatch unchanged]
    C -- yes --> A[analyzer leg: read failed-run logs, one analysis call]
    A --> V{structured verdict}
    V -- transient --> RES[resume retries; reset counter on next success; optional backoff]
    V -- deterministic-infra --> P[park: label sm:leg-blocked + ONE diagnostic comment]
    A -- analyzer itself errors --> D
```

1. **Trigger**: consecutive failures with the same normalized signature
   (issue + workflow scope) reach `failureAnalysis.afterFailures`. Below the
   threshold, behavior is exactly today's blind retry — transient outages
   never even trigger analysis.
2. **Analyzer leg**: a small AI leg (one analysis call; JSRunner-friendly
   scripting around it) whose input is the contextual reports + the failed
   runs' logs for those failures. Output is structured:
   `{ classification: "transient" | "deterministic-infra", confidence,
   suspected_root_cause, evidence: [log lines], suggested_fix }`.
3. **On `transient`**: resume normal retries immediately (optionally with a
   backoff multiplier on the retry interval — config knob
   `failureAnalysis.backoff`, default off); the signature counter resets on
   the next successful leg.
4. **On `deterministic-infra`**: park — label the issue `sm:leg-blocked`
   (name configurable in SM config), post ONE diagnostic comment (root
   cause + evidence + suggested fix), and stop re-dispatching that issue.
   Re-dispatch resumes when the label is removed or the issue is
   re-assigned — i.e. a human or a landed fix decides.
5. **Fail-safe**: if the analyzer leg itself errors (AI unavailable, parse
   failure), fall through to blind retry — a broken analyzer must never stop
   retries.
6. **Setup-phase prior**: the failing step's phase (issue 01) goes into the
   analyzer input; repeated `setup`-phase failures are near-certainly
   deterministic, repeated `ai-work` failures usually transient — the
   analyzer weighs this, the config does not hard-code it.

## Implementation pointers

- SM dispatch loop: `js/machineSmAgent.js` (tracker ops via
  `js/common/smProvider.js`); the analyzer is dispatched like any small leg,
  not in-process AI.
- Analyzer prompt + structured-output contract follow the existing verdict
  protocol style (`js/common/reviewVerdicts.js` is the house pattern for
  machine-validated structured AI output).
- Signature counting reuses the normalizer from issue 01 — no second
  implementation.
- Tests: a scripted-provider harness (in-memory runs, no external calls)
  replaying the acceptance matrix below — no live dispatching needed to
  verify the state machine.
- Missing config → feature disabled silently (no behavior change until the
  owner enables it in the SM config); malformed config → hard validation
  error at SM start (house rule).

## Acceptance criteria

1. `afterFailures = 4`: three identical failures → no analyzer dispatch,
   blind retry unchanged; the fourth dispatches the analyzer once.
2. `transient` verdict → retries continue without any label/comment spam;
   counter resets after a success; a NEW identical streak re-triggers
   analysis only after the threshold again.
3. `deterministic-infra` verdict → issue labeled `sm:leg-blocked`, exactly
   ONE diagnostic comment, no further re-dispatch of that issue.
4. Removing the label (or re-assigning) resumes dispatch.
5. Analyzer leg crashes → blind retry continues, nothing parked, one
   warning logged.
6. Different-signature failures never merge into one streak.
7. Config: missing → disabled silently; malformed → hard error at SM start.
8. Scripted-provider tests cover criteria 1–5.

## Out of scope

Backoff policies beyond the simple multiplier knob; cross-issue storm
detection (a digest-level concern, separate issue); auto-fixing the root
cause — the analyzer diagnoses, it does not repair."

{
  "name": "JSRunner",
  "params": {
    "jsPath": "agents/js/machineSmAgent.js",
    "jobParams": {
      "repo": "epam/dmtools-dart",
      "scm": {
        "provider": "github"
      },
      "dryRun": false,
      "maxConcurrentRuns": 1,
      "maxReworkRounds": 2,
      "workflowFile": "ai-teammate.yml",
      "branchPrefix": "ai/gh-",
      "agentHandle": "ai-teammate",
      "issueLimit": 50
    }
  }
}===
# AI Teammate — thin stub over the factory home (dmtools-agentic-workflows),
# SELF-HOSTED ENGINE: this repo IS the dmtools-agents engine, so factory_ref
# rides the triggering commit — the factory always executes the exact tree
# under development.
#
# ALL logic lives in IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/
# factory-teammate.yml (guard, legs, verdict, sessions, memory). This file
# carries the repository event triggers + the call only.
#
# Gate: the loop starts when a human ASSIGNS an issue to `ai-teammate`.
# Secrets via `secrets: inherit`: SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN (present), plus
# ZAI_CODE_KEY / KIMI_REVIEW_KEY when the fa/zai runners are used.
#
# gh-676 (2026-10-03): while this file was unparseable (#669 residue —
# duplicate permission keys, fixed in #671), GitHub kept a stale push-event
# registration: every machine-sm state-publish push to `factory-data`
# spawned an instant-fail event=push run with zero jobs ("the phantom").
# This comment block is the standard cure — a no-op touch of the file: the
# default-branch blob change forces GitHub to re-index the registration
# from the real triggers below. There is NO push trigger by design; the
# trigger set (issues + workflow_dispatch only) and the duplicate-key
# ban are guarded by js/unit-tests/test_workflowLint.js.
#
# gh-1076 (live 2026-10-19, #1074): ONE owner assign spawned THREE runs —
# the `assigned` event plus two `labeled` events from dmtools-factory-
# bot's OWN consequence labels. `types: [assigned, labeled]` fired on
# EVERY label write, so the workflow re-triggered itself on its own
# status:* consequences; gh-1065 dedup made the duplicates self-skip, but
# each still started a run, occupied the concurrency group, spammed the
# run list and cost a probe. GitHub cannot filter label names in `on:`,
# and a job-level `if:` still starts and LISTS the run (the owner's
# explicit complaint) — so the event trigger is `assigned` ONLY.
# Label-driven pickup (arming labels agent:*) continues through the SM
# tick's workflow_dispatch path (gh-1028 dedup), the governed lane.
name: AI Teammate

# gh-1065: the title carries the LEG for every path — the dispatch input
# leg directly, and for event-path runs the strongest arming label on the
# issue (rework > review > pr_approved → review > dev). legOfRunName
# (js/common/teammateEventDedup.js) parses the trailing token, so a
# COMPLETED owner stays title-precise: the strict completed-owner leg rule
# (a leg-less completed run never swallows a KNOWN new leg) can only work
# when real leg runs carry their leg in the title.
# gh-1076: the trailing `|| github.event.label.name` fallback is gone with
# the labeled trigger — labeled events can no longer start this workflow,
# and assigned/dispatch events resolve their leg from the labels above.
# gh-1075: a PR-anchored dispatch ALSO carries the `· pr-<N>` anchor right
# after the issue slot, BEFORE the leg — the gh-1075 fork path always
# backfills inputs.pr, and the SM's pull-keyed leg probe
# (branchLegGuard.hasActiveLegRunForPull) keys on this whole-token anchor
# to suppress a second rework arm on the same fork PR. The anchor sits
# BEFORE the trailing-leg token on purpose: stubTailLegOf (the teammate:
# title family in legOfRunName) parses the leg at the END of the title,
# and the gh-1065 completed-owner leg precision depends on it.
run-name: "teammate: ${{ github.event_name }} #${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue }}${{ (github.event.inputs.pr || '') != '' && format(' · pr-{0}', github.event.inputs.pr) || '' }} ${{ github.event.inputs.leg || (contains(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, 'agent:rework') && 'rework') || (contains(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, 'agent:review') && 'review') || (contains(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, 'pr_approved') && 'review') || (contains(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, 'agent:dev') && 'dev') || (contains(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, 'agent:develop') && 'dev') }}"

on:
  # gh-1076: `assigned` ONLY — see the header. The labeled trigger used to
  # re-fire this workflow on the factory's own consequence labels.
  issues:
    types: [assigned]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      issue:
        description: 'Issue number (for dispatch runs)'
        type: string
      leg:
        description: 'Which leg to run'
        type: choice
        # gh-1352: polish — the bounded suggestion-only lap the disposition
        # loop dispatches on an approved BLOCKED head (top-K threads,
        # once-per-head, instability-budgeted).
        options: [dev, review, rework, polish]
      reason:
        description: 'Why (audit trail)'
        type: string
      pr:
        description: 'PR number for PR-anchored runs (review leg on PRs born without an issue, #687)'
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''
      checkout_ref:
        description: 'gh-1075/gh-1096: refs/pull/<N>/head for fork-PR legs (empty = dispatch ref)'
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''

permissions:
  # The factory (factory-teammate.yml@e611e5f) requests this set and a
  # reusable workflow cannot RAISE rights above its caller — the stub must
  # grant the ceiling or every dispatch startup-fails (live dmtools-agents
  # 2026-10-03: 'requesting actions: write, contents: write, issues: write,
  # pull-requests: write, but is only allowed contents: read' — the issue-
  # driven dev lane never ran in this repo).
  actions: write
  contents: write
  issues: write
  pull-requests: write

concurrency:
  group: ai-teammate-${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue || (github.event.inputs.pr && format('pr-{0}', github.event.inputs.pr)) || github.run_id }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  # gh-1065 (live 2026-10-18, issues #1040–#1043 / #1061): one human action
  # (assign, or assign-while-labels-change) emits MULTIPLE issues events and
  # each event started its own run — two per issue, three on #1061, the
  # owner hand-cancelling duplicates. The gh-1028 dedup guards the SM
  # dispatch path only; this job is the missing event-path gate. It probes
  # the repo's ai-teammate.yml runs (per-status gh api fan-out, smAgent
  # parity) and lets the `teammate` call fire only when no OLDER run for
  # the same issue + leg is in flight or freshly completed. Probe errors
  # FAIL OPEN (AC3): a broken check writes proceed=true so the only trigger
  # of a burst is never silently swallowed. The decision itself is the
  # unit-tested pure module js/common/teammateEventDedup.js (AC4) — this
  # step is transport only. The probe short-circuits BEFORE any API call
  # for workflow_dispatch (SM-side gh-1028 governs it) and non-teammate
  # assignees. gh-1076: with the `labeled` trigger removed, the labeled
  # preflight went with it — labeled events can no longer reach this job.
  dedup:
    name: Event-path dedup probe (gh-1065)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # gh-1065 rework (review thread — gh-1029 zero-burn parity): this gate
    # MIRRORS the teammate call gate below. Rejected events execute ZERO
    # jobs: the run concludes failure (the gh-676 phantom pattern) and —
    # because only conclusion 'success' owns the freshness window — can
    # never suppress a trigger for an issue whose leg never ran.
    # gh-1076: the `labeled` trigger is gone (the gate's labeled mirror
    # branch went with it), so the remaining event path is `assigned`
    # addressed to ai-teammate; the dispatch path skips the probe by
    # preflight below.
    if: >-
      github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' ||
      (github.event_name == 'issues' &&
       github.event.action == 'assigned' &&
       contains(github.event.issue.assignees.*.login, 'ai-teammate'))
    outputs:
      proceed: ${{ steps.probe.outputs.proceed }}
      audit: ${{ steps.probe.outputs.audit }}
    steps:

# Machine SM — thin stub over the FROZEN machine loop
# (IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows, reusable).
#
# Same freeze contract as dmtools-dart's machine-sm.yml: the workflow is
# pinned to an immutable SHA; agent code and the dmtools CLI resolve from
# RELEASES at run time via this repo's variables:
#   vars.AGENTS_VERSION  — dmtools-agents release tag ('latest' default)
#   vars.DMTOOLS_VERSION — dmtools-dart CLI release tag ('latest' default)
# Bump a version = repo-settings edit, never a workflow edit.
# NO caller-side concurrency: the factory owns the `machine-sm` group.

name: 'Machine SM'

run-name: >-
  🧹 SM ${{
    github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && 'manual tick' ||
    format('tick {0}', github.event.schedule || '') }}${{
  github.event.inputs.dryRun == 'true' && ' (dry)' || '' }}

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '*/10 * * * *'   # short ticks — the engine idles when busy
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      dryRun:
        description: 'Log the plan, perform no action'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: true

permissions:
  contents: write         # checkout + silent update-branch pushes
  issues: write           # labels + close-issue safety net
  pull-requests: write    # update-branch + merge
  checks: write           # bridge-free validation stamps
  actions: write          # workflow_dispatch on the teammate workflow

jobs:
  sm:
    # Pinned to the immutable SHA of IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows main
    # (the frozen machine-loop home; bump the SHA only together with the
    # matching loop change).
    uses: IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-sm.yml@main
    with:
      # No .dmtools/config.js in this repo — the machine logins ride the
      # deployment-level input (#687, gh-728), exactly like the factory's
      # contract. Comma-separated LIST: the agent harness bot AND the CI
      # bot — github-actions[bot] authors its own PRs (live fa PR #1249)
      # and must ride the machine path (owner directive 2026-10-05).
      machine-author: 'ai-teammate,github-actions[bot],dmtools-factory-bot'
      # This repo dispatches no CI on PR heads (docs checks only) — the SM
      # leaves validation to the event-driven merge bot and labels.
      ci-workflow: ''
      # Manual ticks default to dry; cron ticks run live.
      dryRun: ${{ github.event.inputs.dryRun || 'false' }}
      # Factory-state snapshot → factory-data branch (board: site/factory,
      # third tab; fa machine-sm.yml parity — transport lives in
      # js/factoryState.js, publishing is opt-in per factory).
      # gh-1108: tokensAsset pins the agents factory's OWN tokens stream —
      # fetchTokensFromBranch defaults to the fixed fa-side asset, so
      # without this knob the agents tick would fetch (and silently
      # publish) the WRONG factory's rows on any shared branch.
      state-publish: '{"channel":"release","tag":"factory-data","asset":"agents-state.json","tokensAsset":"agents-tokens.json"}'
      # Silent branch updates: input channel (github.token via secrets/in
      # blocks arrives empty through a reusable call — live-verified).
      silent-token: ${{ github.token }}
    secrets:
      SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN }}
      # App auth (awf#52): minted installation token wins over the PAT
      # inside the factory when both secrets are present.
      APP_ID: ${{ secrets.APP_ID }}
      APP_PRIVATE_KEY: ${{ secrets.APP_PRIVATE_KEY }}
      SILENT_GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SILENT_GH_TOKEN }}

/**

 * SERIALIZES the duplicates into queued no-op burns — it never drops them.
 *
 * This module is the missing gate: an issues-event run proceeds only when
 * NO OTHER ai-teammate run for the SAME issue + leg is in flight (active
 * status, gh-1028 stale-zombie parity) or freshly completed (a fulfilled
 * leg owns a short freshness window — burst duplicates of one action land

 *  - IN-FLIGHT owners: an unknown leg on either side wildcards. Event-path
 *    burst titles cannot be told apart; an in-flight owner of the same
 *    issue is almost certainly the same human action (AC1/AC4).
 *  - COMPLETED owners: the wildcard is GONE. A completed owner with an
 *    unknown leg suppressing a KNOWN-leg event is exactly the sequential-
 *    human-action case (assign at T, deliberate agent:review at T+6min) —
 *    it proceeds. A completed owner suppresses only when both legs are
 *    unknown (a second bare assign inside the window is burst noise) or
 *    both known and equal (the concurrency-released burst duplicate).
 *
 * Tie-break (AC1, exactly one survivor): only a run that is STRICTLY OLDER
 * than the probing run suppresses it (run_number order, created_at
 * fallback). Burst runs are created milliseconds apart in run_number order,
 * so the earliest always proceeds and every later duplicate of the burst
 * drops — regardless of which probe executes first.

# Integration-readiness concerns — gh-1366

## 1. The `analyze` leg executes in the factory workflow repo (external)

- **What the PR does**: the machine SM (`js/machineSmAgent.js`) dispatches the analyzer as a normal machine leg (`dispatchLeg(issue, 'analyze', reason, workflowFile)`) at the exact `failureAnalysis.afterFailures` crossing, and lists `analyze` in the `workflow_dispatch` leg choices of both `.github/workflows/ai-teammate.yml` and `workflows/ai-teammate.yml.template`.
- **What is missing**: the ai-teammate workflow is a thin stub over the frozen factory loop (`IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows` → `factory-teammate.yml`), which owns per-leg execution. It does not yet handle `leg=analyze` — no factory job reads the issue's failure reports, runs the one AI analysis call, or stamps the `<!-- dmtools:failure-verdict {...} -->` marker comment this PR's contract defines (`js/common/failureAnalyzer.js`).
- **What is needed to make it work**: add the `analyze` leg handler to `factory-teammate.yml` in the factory repo. The leg reads the issue's gh-1363 failure comments (`failure-signature:` lines), performs ONE analysis call, and posts `buildFailureVerdictComment(record)` as a machine-authored comment (the machine author must be in the SM's `machineAuthor` allowlist — `machine-sm.yml` already passes `ai-teammate,github-actions[bot],dmtools-factory-bot`).
- **Safety meanwhile**: the feature is OFF until the owner sets `failureAnalysis` in the SM config (missing config → disabled silently). Even if enabled before the factory leg lands, the fail-safe holds: a failed/absent analyzer verdict means no marker, no consumption, and blind retries continue (AC5) — the loop cannot stop, only the analysis benefit is missing.

## 2. `failureAnalysis.backoff` is validated but has no SM-side effect yet

- **What the PR does**: accepts and validates the knob (number ≥ 1, default 1 = off) per the ticket, and documents it.
- **What is missing**: applying a multiplier to the retry interval — the machine SM has no per-issue retry interval (the cron tick cadence is the interval), so a real backoff needs per-issue tick-marker machinery (the quota-park pattern).
- **What is needed**: a follow-up that applies the multiplier on the tick cadence after a `transient` verdict (out of scope here per the ticket: "Backoff policies beyond the simple multiplier knob").

arguments.content:
### What changed
Added the AI failure-analyzer leg to the machine SM's failure path (`js/machineSmAgent.js` + new pure contract `js/common/failureAnalyzer.js`): when consecutive same-signature failures (gh-1363 normalizer, reused — no second implementation) reach `failureAnalysis.afterFailures` (default 4), the SM dispatches an `analyze` leg instead of the blind retry; a `transient` verdict resumes retries, a `deterministic-infra` verdict parks the issue (`sm:leg-blocked` label + exactly ONE diagnostic comment) until the label is removed or the issue is re-assigned.

### Key decisions
- Analysis triggers at the EXACT threshold crossing (`effectiveStreakCount === afterFailures`), with analyzer verdicts consuming their analyzed streak prefix via the machine-parseable `<!-- dmtools:failure-verdict -->` marker — a crashed analyzer therefore can neither park nor re-dispatch itself every tick (fail-safe, AC5)
- Verdict markers follow the reviewVerdicts house protocol and are trusted only from machine identities (fail-closed without a configured allowlist); the park comment's ONE-comment idempotency keys on a machine marker, never text
- Every stage fails safe: disabled/unreadable/unparseable leaves the loop byte-identical to today (gitlab provider without the issue-comment primitive included)
- Config: missing → disabled silently; malformed → hard validation error at SM start; `machineSm.failureAnalysis` overrides `jobParams` knob-by-knob; `analyze` added to the workflow_dispatch leg choices (stub + template)

### How to verify
```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_failureAnalyzer.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_machineSmAgent.json   # scripted-provider replay of AC1–AC7
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smProvider.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json              # 8800 passed, 0 failed
```

<details><summary>Failure path</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    F[leg fails] --> R[gh-1363 report: signature line on the issue]
```
